description: One change to the system, who made it, who approved it, and how to undo it. This is the IT general control an auditor tests by sampling — pick five changes, show me who approved each — and an operation that cannot answer for one of the five has failed the control for all of them. Most rows here are written by this app about itself: a permission granted, a compliance rule enabled, a tool switch flipped. The ones somebody types are the changes made outside it.

fields.description: What KIND of change. A closed list because the change management report groups on it, and because the categories are what an auditor's sample is drawn from — 'show me five permission changes' is a question the list has to be able to answer.
fields.label: Change Type
fields.options:
Configuration
DocType Schema
Permission
Role Assignment
User Account
Integration
Compliance Rule
Tool Switch
Data Correction
Infrastructure
Other

fields.description: What changed, in one line somebody scanning a year of these can read.
fields.label: Title

fields.description: When it happened — not when it was written down. The two differ for anything recorded after the fact, and the report says so rather than quietly treating the record's creation as the event.
fields.label: Change Date

fields.description: How much is riding on it. Drives nothing automatically — it is what makes a sample of five changes a sample somebody chose rather than the first five in the table.
fields.label: Risk Level

fields.description: Where the row came from. `MCP Tool` rows are written by this app about its own privileged calls and are the ones an auditor can trust were not curated; `Manual` rows are somebody typing up a change made elsewhere, which is the honest label for them.
fields.label: Source
fields.options:
Manual
MCP Tool
Migration
Desk
External

fields.description: The change in enough detail that somebody who was not there could tell what the system did before and does now.
fields.label: Description

fields.description: The audit row for the call that made this change, when this app made it. It is what turns 'somebody says they changed a permission' into 'the server recorded this call, with these arguments, at this time'.
fields.label: MCP Action Log

fields.description: NOT REQUIRED IS A DECISION AND IS RECORDED AS ONE. A change that needed nobody's approval is a defensible answer; a change whose approval nobody can find is not, and the two must not look the same in a sample.
fields.label: Approval Status

fields.description: Who approved it. The control refuses this being the same person who made the change — that is the whole of what change approval means, and a farm where one person does both records it as a known exception rather than by naming themselves twice.
fields.label: Approved By

fields.description: How this would be undone if it went wrong. Asked at the moment it is cheap to answer, because the moment it is needed is the moment nobody can think.
fields.label: Rollback Plan

fields.description: Whether the change was tested before it went live.
fields.label: Tested

name: Change Management Log
